text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today after jumping nearly 6.5% yesterday, but the stock remains up sharply over the past two weeks as oil prices have surged on Middle East tensions. Brent crude has climbed above $126, driven by Houthi militant attacks on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure and airports—threats to global oil supply that benefit major oil producers like ConocoPhillips. The small pullback today appears to be profit-taking after a strong run rather than a reversal in the underlying trend.

The broader rally reflects genuine supply risk: Iran-backed attacks have intensified, and both Saudi Arabia and Iran have signaled potential further escalation, keeping investors focused on potential disruptions to Middle Eastern production. Oil price strength of this magnitude—Brent up roughly 50% since mid-September based on the price data—is the main driver of ConocoPhillips' two-week gain.
